paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : GPQA confidence vs. accuracy

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and various accuracy metrics. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence" with a linear scale ranging from 0.91 to 0.99, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and also has a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The blue line with circle markers and error bars, representing "Final Accuracy", is solid and begins at approximately 0.90 at an initial confidence of 0.91 and ends near 0.90 at 0.99, peaking at around 0.93 with an Accuracy of approximately 1.0. The orange line with diamond markers and error bars, representing "∆ Accuracy", is dashed and starts at around 0.55, declining to about 0.18 by 0.99, with a notable drop after 0.97. The green line with square markers and error bars, representing "Initial Accuracy", is dashed and begins at approximately 0.38 at 0.91, increasing and peaking at around 0.85 at 0.98 before declining slightly to around 0.75 at 0.99. The orange dashed line and green dashed line intersect each other just before x =0.93, x=0.94 and x=0.97. All three lines include error bars, indicating variability at each data point. There are legends provided on top of the plot to match different line styles to their labels.
